newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait parliament panel rejects budget proposal.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait parliament panel rejects budget proposal.

text.p: A Kuwaiti parliamentary committee has rejected the government's 1997-98 (July-June) budget proposal for assuming a rise in revenue through higher tariffs, a leading MP said on Saturday.

The oil state, which offers nationals a cradle-to-grave welfare system including heavily subsidised basic services, is not allowed to raise charges for public services without prior parliamentary approval.
"We suspended the budget discussion," said Nasser al-Sanea, head of parliament's finance committee. "It is rejected because the government is assuming higher income from raised tariffs."

He told Reuters that although non-oil revenue in the 1997-98 budget is unchanged from the budget for the current fiscal year to end-June at 645 million dinars ($2.12 billion), the proposed budget assumes 200 million dinars in revenue from higher rates for basic services.

"This is illegal. The government is assuming that the law (which puts a lid on prices) will be changed," Sanea said. "Changing a law takes a while...This budget, with such assumptions, is rejected and we have sent it back."

The proposed 4.37 billion dinar 1997-98 budget forecasts a net deficit of 1.17 billion dinars. By law 10 percent of total revenue is placed in an overseas investment fund, raising the projected deficit by a further 320 million dinars.

The 4.21 billion dinar 1996-97 budget carries a projected net deficit of 1.21 billion dinars and a gross deficit of 1.51 billion. The shortfall is expected to be largely covered by higher world oil prices which earlier this year rose more than $5 a barrel above budget projections.

The proposed 1997-98 budget, which has to be approved by parliament and the head of state before it becomes law, put oil revenue at 2.56 billion dinars, almost unchanged from the budget for the current fiscal year.

Although oil prices dropped in recent weeks, they are still higher than Kuwait's budget estimates. The OPEC member, which produces about two million barrels of oil a day, calculates oil revenue for Kuwaiti crudes on a conservative average barrel price of $13.
The world benchmark Brent crude oil price is about $20 a barrel.
